terms.gloss: turn a cartwheel, roll oneself over like a wheel
terms.grammar: volvō with the reflexive; in modum with the genitive
terms.comment: A description of ours: in modum with the genitive, “in the manner of”, and sē volvere, roll oneself. We have found no word for a cartwheel in Lewis & Short, the loci collections, Traupman, or Levi–Bini; Latin has words for the tumbler (petaurista), not for this turn. Latin says it with a verb here; there is no noun to give.

phrases.latin: Spectā mē; in modum rotae mē volvō!
phrases.english: Watch me; I’m doing a cartwheel!

phrases.latin: Prīmum manūs in terram pōne, deinde crūra in altum jace.
phrases.english: First put your hands on the ground, then throw your legs up.

sources: Lewis & Short: rota · Lewis & Short: volvo
